passages.text: Many have undertaken to compose an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us, just as they were handed down to us by the initial eyewitnesses and servants of the word.
passages.sermon:
Many people have tried to write an account.
They wrote about the things that happened among us.
These things have been fulfilled.
The first eyewitnesses saw these things.
The first eyewitnesses served the word.
They handed down these things to us.
passages.original: Ἐπειδήπερ πολλοὶ ἐπεχείρησαν ἀνατάξασθαι διήγησιν περὶ τῶν πεπληροφορημένων ἐν ἡμῖν πραγμάτων καθὼς παρέδοσαν ἡμῖν οἱ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς αὐτόπται καὶ ὑπηρέται γενόμενοι τοῦ λόγου

passages.text: Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus, so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
passages.sermon:
I am writing to you, most excellent Theophilus.
I have carefully investigated everything from the beginning.
I have followed all these things closely.
I decided to write an orderly account for you.
I want you to know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
passages.original: ἔδοξε κἀμοὶ παρηκολουθηκότι ἄνωθεν πᾶσιν ἀκριβῶς καθεξῆς σοι γράψαι κράτιστε Θεόφιλε ἵνα ἐπιγνῷς περὶ ὧν κατηχήθης λόγων τὴν ἀσφάλειαν

passages.text: In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and whose wife Elizabeth was a daughter of Aaron.
passages.sermon:
Herod was king of Judea.
During his reign, there was a priest named Zechariah.
Zechariah belonged to the priestly division of Abijah.
Zechariah had a wife named Elizabeth.
Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρῴδου βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἱερεύς τις ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβιά καὶ γυνὴ αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων Ἀαρών καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτῆς Ἐλισάβετ

passages.text: Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest.
Elizabeth was his wife.
Both Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous before God.
They obeyed all the commandments of the Lord.
They followed all the decrees of the Lord.
They lived blamelessly.
passages.original: ἦσαν δὲ δίκαιοι ἀμφότεροι ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ πορευόμενοι ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἐντολαῖς καὶ δικαιώμασιν τοῦ Κυρίου ἄμεμπτοι

passages.text: But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well along in years.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest.
Elizabeth was his wife.
Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
They had no children.
Elizabeth could not have children.
Elizabeth was barren.
Zechariah and Elizabeth were both old.
They were both advanced in years.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἦν αὐτοῖς τέκνον καθότι ἦν ἡ Ἐλισάβετ στεῖρα καὶ ἀμφότεροι προβεβηκότες ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῶν ἦσαν

passages.text: One day while Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God, he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest.
He belonged to a division of priests.
One day, his division was on duty.
Zechariah served as priest before God.
The priests had a custom.
They chose by lot who would perform certain duties.
Zechariah was chosen by lot.
He was chosen to enter the temple of the Lord.
He was chosen to burn incense in the temple.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἱερατεύειν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ τάξει τῆς ἐφημερίας αὐτοῦ ἔναντι τοῦ Θεοῦ κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς ἱερατείας ἔλαχε τοῦ θυμιᾶσαι εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: And at the hour of the incense offering, the whole congregation was praying outside.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered together.
They formed a large crowd.
They stood outside the temple.
It was the time for burning incense.
All the people prayed together at that hour.
passages.original: καὶ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος ἦν τοῦ λαοῦ προσευχόμενον ἔξω τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ θυμιάματος

passages.text: Just then an angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
passages.sermon: An angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah.\r\nThe angel stood at the right side of the altar of incense.
passages.original: Ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἑστὼς ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τοῦ θυμιάματος

passages.text: When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and gripped with fear.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest.
Zechariah saw the angel of the Lord.
Zechariah became startled.
Fear came over Zechariah.
passages.original: καὶ ἐταράχθη Ζαχαρίας ἰδών καὶ φόβος ἐπέπεσεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to give him the name John.
passages.sermon:
An angel of the Lord spoke to Zechariah.
The angel said, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah.
God has heard your prayer.
Your wife Elizabeth will have a son.
You will name him John.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ ἄγγελος Μὴ φοβοῦ Ζαχαρία διότι εἰσηκούσθη ἡ δέησίς σου καὶ ἡ γυνή σου Ἐλισάβετ γεννήσει υἱόν σοι καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰωάννην

passages.text: He will be a joy and delight to you, and many will rejoice at his birth, for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He shall never take wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah, you will have a son.
Your son will bring you joy.
Your son will bring you delight.
Many people will rejoice when your son is born.
Your son will be great before the Lord.
Your son will not drink wine.
Your son will not drink strong drink.
The Holy Spirit will fill your son.
The Holy Spirit will fill him even before he is born.
passages.original: καὶ ἔσται χαρά σοι καὶ ἀγαλλίασις καὶ πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τῇ γενέσει αὐτοῦ χαρήσονται ἔσται γὰρ μέγας ἐνώπιον τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ οἶνον καὶ σίκερα οὐ μὴ πίῃ καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου πλησθήσεται ἔτι ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Many of the sons of Israel he will turn back to the Lord their God.
passages.sermon: John will turn many people of Israel back to the Lord.\r\nThe Lord is their God.\r\nJohn will lead many Israelites to return to God.
passages.original: καὶ πολλοὺς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐπιστρέψει ἐπὶ Κύριον τὸν Θεὸν αὐτῶν

passages.text: And he will go on before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous—to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
passages.sermon:
He will go before the Lord.
He will have the spirit and power of Elijah.
He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children.
He will turn the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous.
He will make a people ready for the Lord.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτὸς προελεύσεται ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ δυνάμει Ἠλίου ἐπιστρέψαι καρδίας πατέρων ἐπὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀπειθεῖς ἐν φρονήσει δικαίων ἑτοιμάσαι Κυρίῳ λαὸν κατεσκευασμένον

passages.text: “How can I be sure of this?” Zechariah asked the angel. “I am an old man, and my wife is well along in years.”
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest of Israel.
Zechariah spoke to the angel.
Zechariah asked a question.
He said, “How can I be sure of this?”
Zechariah explained his doubt.
He said, “I am an old man.”
He also said, “My wife is well along in years.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν Ζαχαρίας πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον Κατὰ τί γνώσομαι τοῦτο ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι πρεσβύτης καὶ ἡ γυνή μου προβεβηκυῖα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτῆς

passages.text: “I am Gabriel,” replied the angel. “I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
passages.sermon:
The angel spoke to Zechariah.
The angel said, “I am Gabriel.”
Gabriel stands in the presence of God.
God sent Gabriel to Zechariah.
Gabriel came to speak to Zechariah.
Gabriel came to bring Zechariah good news.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα

passages.text: And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.”
passages.sermon:
Gabriel is an angel who stands in the presence of God.
Gabriel spoke to Zechariah in the temple.
Gabriel said, “You will be silent.”
Gabriel said, “You will not be able to speak.”
This will last until the day these things happen.
This will happen because you did not believe my words.
My words will come true at their proper time.”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔσῃ σιωπῶν καὶ μὴ δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας γένηται ταῦτα ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἐπίστευσας τοῖς λόγοις μου οἵτινες πληρωθήσονται εἰς τὸν καιρὸν αὐτῶν

passages.text: Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he took so long in the temple.
passages.sermon: The people waited for Zechariah.\r\nThey wondered why Zechariah stayed so long in the temple.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν ὁ λαὸς προσδοκῶν τὸν Ζαχαρίαν καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐν τῷ χρονίζειν ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτόν

passages.text: When he came out and was unable to speak to them, they realized he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them but remained speechless.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest.
He came out of the temple.
He could not speak to the people.
The people saw that Zechariah could not speak.
They understood that Zechariah had seen a vision in the temple.
Zechariah kept making signs to the people.
He stayed unable to speak.
passages.original: ἐξελθὼν δὲ οὐκ ἐδύνατο λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν ὅτι ὀπτασίαν ἑώρακεν ἐν τῷ ναῷ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διανεύων αὐτοῖς καὶ διέμενεν κωφός

passages.text: And when the days of his service were complete, he returned home.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was a priest.
He served in the temple.
His time of service ended.
Zechariah went home.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἐπλήσθησαν αἱ ἡμέραι τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After these days, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant and for five months remained in seclusion. She declared, “The Lord has done this for me. In these days He has shown me favor and taken away my disgrace among the people.”
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was his wife.
After these days, Elizabeth became pregnant.
Elizabeth stayed in seclusion for five months.
Elizabeth said, “The Lord has done this for me.”
She said, “In these days He has shown me favor.”
She said, “He has taken away my disgrace among the people.”
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταύτας τὰς ἡμέρας συνέλαβεν Ἐλισάβετ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ περιέκρυβεν ἑαυτὴν μῆνας πέντε λέγουσα ὅτι Οὕτως μοι πεποίηκεν Κύριος ἐν ἡμέραις αἷς ἐπεῖδεν ἀφελεῖν ὄνειδός μου ἐν ἀνθρώποις

passages.text: In the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin pledged in marriage to a man named Joseph, who was of the house of David. And the virgin’s name was Mary.
passages.sermon:
God sent the angel Gabriel.
This happened in the sixth month.
Gabriel went to a town in Galilee.
The town was called Nazareth.
Gabriel went to a young woman there.
She was a virgin.
She was pledged to marry a man named Joseph.
Joseph belonged to the house of David.
The virgin’s name was Mary.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ μηνὶ τῷ ἕκτῳ ἀπεστάλη ὁ ἄγγελος Γαβριὴλ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ᾗ ὄνομα Ναζαρὲθ πρὸς παρθένον ἐμνηστευμένην ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰωσὴφ ἐξ οἴκου Δαυὶδ καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς παρθένου Μαριάμ

passages.text: The angel appeared to her and said, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you.”
passages.sermon:
God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary.
Mary was a virgin.
Mary lived in Nazareth, a town in Galilee.
Gabriel entered where Mary was.
Gabriel spoke to Mary.
Gabriel said, “Greetings, you are highly favored.”
Gabriel said, “The Lord is with you.”
passages.original: καὶ εἰσελθὼν πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη ὁ Κύριος μετὰ σοῦ

passages.text: Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be.
passages.sermon:
Mary heard the angel’s words.
Mary felt very troubled.
Mary wondered about the greeting.
Mary did not know what the greeting meant.
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ διεταράχθη καὶ διελογίζετο ποταπὸς εἴη ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος

passages.text: So the angel told her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
passages.sermon: An angel spoke to Mary.\r\nThe angel said, “Do not be afraid, Mary.\r\nYou have found favor with God.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ἄγγελος αὐτῇ Μὴ φοβοῦ Μαριάμ εὗρες γὰρ χάριν παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus.
passages.sermon: Mary, you will become pregnant.\r\nYou will give birth to a son.\r\nYou must name him Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ συλλήμψῃ ἐν γαστρὶ καὶ τέξῃ υἱόν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give Him the throne of His father David, and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus will be great.
People will call Jesus the Son of the Most High God.
The Lord God will give Jesus the throne of David, who was His ancestor.
Jesus will rule over the house of Jacob forever.
Jesus’ kingdom will never end.
passages.original: οὗτος ἔσται μέγας καὶ Υἱὸς Ὑψίστου κληθήσεται καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς τὸν θρόνον Δαυὶδ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ βασιλεύσει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰακὼβ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας καὶ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔσται τέλος

passages.text: “How can this be,” Mary asked the angel, “since I am a virgin?”
passages.sermon:
Mary was a young woman.
Mary had not been with a man.
Mary spoke to the angel.
Mary asked the angel a question.
Mary said, “How can this happen?”
Mary said, “I am a virgin.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ Μαριὰμ πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον Πῶς ἔσται τοῦτο ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω

passages.text: The angel replied, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. So the Holy One to be born will be called the Son of God.
passages.sermon:
The angel spoke to Mary.
The angel answered her question.
The Holy Spirit will come upon you, Mary.
The power of the Most High God will cover you.
Because of this, the child to be born will be holy.
He will be called the Son of God.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῇ Πνεῦμα Ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ καὶ δύναμις Ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι διὸ καὶ τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον κληθήσεται Υἱὸς Θεοῦ

passages.text: Look, even Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son in her old age, and she who was called barren is in her sixth month.
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth is your relative.
Elizabeth has conceived a son.
Elizabeth is old.
People called Elizabeth barren.
Elizabeth is now in her sixth month of pregnancy.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἐλισάβετ ἡ συγγενίς σου καὶ αὐτὴ συνείληφεν υἱὸν ἐν γήρει αὐτῆς καὶ οὗτος μὴν ἕκτος ἐστὶν αὐτῇ τῇ καλουμένῃ στείρᾳ

passages.text: For no word from God will ever fail.”
passages.sermon: God always keeps His word.\r\nNothing is impossible for God.\r\nEvery promise from God will happen.
passages.original: ὅτι οὐκ ἀδυνατήσει παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ πᾶν ῥῆμα

passages.text: “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” Then the angel left her.
passages.sermon:
Mary spoke.
Mary said, "I am the Lord’s servant."
Mary said, "Let it happen to me as you have said."
The angel left Mary.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ Μαριάμ Ἰδοὺ ἡ δούλη Κυρίου γένοιτό μοι κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς ὁ ἄγγελος

passages.text: In those days Mary got ready and hurried to a town in the hill country of Judah, where she entered the home of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
passages.sermon:
Mary was a young woman chosen by God.
In those days, Mary prepared herself quickly.
She traveled with haste to a town in the hill country of Judah.
She entered the house of Zechariah.
She greeted Elizabeth.
passages.original: Ἀναστᾶσα δὲ Μαριὰμ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὴν ὀρεινὴν μετὰ σπουδῆς εἰς πόλιν Ἰούδα καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον Ζαχαρίου καὶ ἠσπάσατο τὴν Ἐλισάβετ

passages.text: When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon: Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting.\r\nThe baby leaped in Elizabeth’s womb.\r\nThe Holy Spirit filled Elizabeth.
passages.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν τὸν ἀσπασμὸν τῆς Μαρίας ἡ Ἐλισάβετ ἐσκίρτησεν τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐπλήσθη Πνεύματος Ἁγίου ἡ Ἐλισάβετ

passages.text: In a loud voice she exclaimed, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She spoke in a loud voice.
She said, “You are blessed among women.
The child in your womb is blessed.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀνεφώνησεν κραυγῇ μεγάλῃ καὶ εἶπεν Εὐλογημένη σὺ ἐν γυναιξίν καὶ εὐλογημένος ὁ καρπὸς τῆς κοιλίας σου

passages.text: And why am I so honored, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was an older woman.
Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Elizabeth spoke to Mary.
Elizabeth said, “Why is this happening to me?”
Elizabeth said, “The mother of my Lord has come to me.”
Elizabeth felt honored.
passages.original: καὶ πόθεν μοι τοῦτο ἵνα ἔλθῃ ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Κυρίου μου πρὸς ἐμέ

passages.text: For as soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy.
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was the mother of John the Baptist.
Mary greeted Elizabeth.
Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting.
The sound of Mary’s greeting entered Elizabeth’s ears.
The baby was inside Elizabeth’s womb.
The baby in Elizabeth’s womb leaped.
The baby leaped with joy.
passages.original: ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡ φωνὴ τοῦ ἀσπασμοῦ σου εἰς τὰ ὦτά μου ἐσκίρτησεν ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει τὸ βρέφος ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ μου

passages.text: Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord’s word to her will be fulfilled.”
passages.sermon:
Mary is the mother of Jesus.
Mary believed what the Lord said to her.
The Lord spoke a promise to Mary.
Mary trusted that the Lord would do what He said.
God will fulfill His word to Mary.
God blesses Mary because she believed Him.
passages.original: καὶ μακαρία ἡ πιστεύσασα ὅτι ἔσται τελείωσις τοῖς λελαλημένοις αὐτῇ παρὰ Κυρίου

passages.text: Then Mary said: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior!
passages.sermon:
Mary spoke.
Mary praised God.
Mary said her soul magnifies the Lord.
Mary said her spirit rejoices in God.
God is her Savior.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν Μαριάμ Μεγαλύνει ἡ ψυχή μου τὸν Κύριον καὶ ἠγαλλίασεν τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπὶ τῷ Θεῷ τῷ Σωτῆρί μου

passages.text: For He has looked with favor on the humble state of His servant. From now on all generations will call me blessed.
passages.sermon: God looked with favor on His servant Mary.\r\nMary was humble.\r\nFrom this time forward, all generations will call Mary blessed.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐπέβλεψεν ἐπὶ τὴν ταπείνωσιν τῆς δούλης αὐτοῦ ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν μακαριοῦσίν με πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί

passages.text: For the Mighty One has done great things for me. Holy is His name.
passages.sermon: God is the Mighty One.\r\nGod has done great things for me.\r\nGod’s name is holy.
passages.original: ὅτι ἐποίησέν μοι μεγάλα ὁ δυνατός καὶ ἅγιον τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: His mercy extends to those who fear Him, from generation to generation.
passages.sermon:
God shows mercy.
God gives mercy to people who fear Him.
God gives mercy to every generation.
God gives mercy again and again, to all who respect Him.
passages.original: καὶ τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ εἰς γενεὰς καὶ γενεὰς τοῖς φοβουμένοις αὐτόν

passages.text: He has performed mighty deeds with His arm; He has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
passages.sermon:
God is mighty.
God uses His power.
God has done great things with His arm.
God acts with strength.
God scatters proud people.
Proud people trust their own thoughts.
God defeats those who are proud in their hearts.
passages.original: Ἐποίησεν κράτος ἐν βραχίονι αὐτοῦ διεσκόρπισεν ὑπερηφάνους διανοίᾳ καρδίας αὐτῶν

passages.text: He has brought down rulers from their thrones, but has exalted the humble.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power.
God brings down rulers from their thrones.
God removes the powerful from their high positions.
God lifts up the humble.
God gives honor to those who are lowly.
passages.original: καθεῖλεν δυνάστας ἀπὸ θρόνων καὶ ὕψωσεν ταπεινούς

passages.text: He has filled the hungry with good things, but has sent the rich away empty.
passages.sermon: God acts with power and mercy.\r\nGod fills the hungry with good things.\r\nGod sends the rich away with nothing.
passages.original: πεινῶντας ἐνέπλησεν ἀγαθῶν καὶ πλουτοῦντας ἐξαπέστειλεν κενούς

passages.text: He has helped His servant Israel, remembering to be merciful, as He promised to our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants forever.”
passages.sermon:
God helped Israel.
Israel is His servant.
God remembered to show mercy.
God promised mercy to our fathers.
God made this promise to Abraham.
God also promised this to Abraham’s descendants.
God’s promise lasts forever.
passages.original: ἀντελάβετο Ἰσραὴλ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ μνησθῆναι ἐλέους καθὼς ἐλάλησεν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν τῷ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: Mary stayed with Elizabeth for about three months and then returned home.
passages.sermon: Mary stayed with Elizabeth.\r\nShe stayed for about three months.\r\nAfter that, Mary returned to her own home.
passages.original: Ἔμεινεν δὲ Μαριὰμ σὺν αὐτῇ ὡς μῆνας τρεῖς καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς

passages.text: When the time came for Elizabeth to have her child, she gave birth to a son.
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was an older woman.
Elizabeth was the wife of Zechariah.
Elizabeth became pregnant by God’s promise.
The time arrived for Elizabeth to give birth.
Elizabeth gave birth to a son.
passages.original: Τῇ δὲ Ἐλισάβετ ἐπλήσθη ὁ χρόνος τοῦ τεκεῖν αὐτήν καὶ ἐγέννησεν υἱόν

passages.text: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was an older woman.
Elizabeth had just given birth to a son.
The Lord showed great mercy to Elizabeth.
Her neighbors heard about this.
Her relatives also heard about this.
They heard that the Lord had been merciful to Elizabeth.
Her neighbors rejoiced with her.
Her relatives rejoiced with her.
passages.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ περίοικοι καὶ οἱ συγγενεῖς αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐμεγάλυνεν Κύριος τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτῆς καὶ συνέχαιρον αὐτῇ

passages.text: On the eighth day, when they came to circumcise the child, they were going to name him after his father Zechariah.
passages.sermon:
Elizabeth was the mother of the child.
\r\nZechariah was the father of the child.
\r\nOn the eighth day, people came.
\r\nThey came to circumcise the child.
\r\nThey planned to name the child Zechariah.
\r\nZechariah was the name of the child’s father.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἦλθον περιτεμεῖν τὸ παιδίον καὶ ἐκάλουν αὐτὸ ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ Ζαχαρίαν

passages.text: But his mother replied, “No! He shall be called John.”
passages.sermon:
His mother spoke.
She answered them.
She said, "No."
She said, "He will be called John."
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεῖσα ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν Οὐχί ἀλλὰ κληθήσεται Ἰωάννης

passages.text: They said to her, “There is no one among your relatives who bears this name.”
passages.sermon:
The people spoke to the child's mother.
They said, "None of your relatives has this name."
No one in your family is called by this name.
You have no relatives named John.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτὴν ὅτι Οὐδείς ἐστιν ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου ὃς καλεῖται τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ

passages.text: So they made signs to his father to find out what he wanted to name the child.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was the father of the child.
The people could not speak with Zechariah directly.
They made signs to Zechariah.
They wanted to know what name Zechariah wanted for the child.
passages.original: ἐνένευον δὲ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ τί ἂν θέλοι καλεῖσθαι αὐτό

passages.text: Zechariah asked for a tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” And they were all amazed.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was the father of the child.
Zechariah could not speak.
Zechariah asked for a tablet.
Zechariah wrote on the tablet.
Zechariah wrote, “His name is John.”
All the people saw what Zechariah wrote.
All the people were amazed.
passages.original: Καὶ αἰτήσας πινακίδιον ἔγραψεν λέγων Ἰωάννης ἐστὶν ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐθαύμασαν πάντες

passages.text: Immediately Zechariah’s mouth was opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak, praising God.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was John’s father.
Zechariah could not speak before this moment.
Suddenly, Zechariah’s mouth opened.
His tongue became free.
Zechariah began to speak.
He praised God.
passages.original: ἀνεῴχθη δὲ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ παραχρῆμα καὶ ἡ γλῶσσα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐλάλει εὐλογῶν τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: All their neighbors were filled with awe, and people throughout the hill country of Judea were talking about these events.
passages.sermon:
All the neighbors saw what happened.
A sense of awe filled every neighbor.
People lived in the hill country of Judea.
Everyone in that region heard about these events.
People talked about everything that happened.
The news spread throughout the whole hill country of Judea.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πάντας φόβος τοὺς περιοικοῦντας αὐτούς καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ὀρεινῇ τῆς Ἰουδαίας διελαλεῖτο πάντα τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα

passages.text: And all who heard this wondered in their hearts and asked, “What then will this child become?” For the Lord’s hand was with him.
passages.sermon:
All the people heard about these things.
They thought deeply about them in their hearts.
They asked, “What will this child become?”
The Lord’s hand was with the child.
passages.original: καὶ ἔθεντο πάντες οἱ ἀκούσαντες ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτῶν λέγοντες Τί ἄρα τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο ἔσται καὶ γὰρ χεὶρ Κυρίου ἦν μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied: “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and redeemed His people.
passages.sermon:
Zechariah was the father of the child.
God filled Zechariah with the Holy Spirit.
Zechariah prophesied.
Zechariah said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel.
The Lord has visited His people.
The Lord has redeemed His people.”
passages.original: Καὶ Ζαχαρίας ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐπλήσθη Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ ἐπροφήτευσεν λέγων Εὐλογητὸς Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ ὅτι ἐπεσκέψατο καὶ ἐποίησεν λύτρωσιν τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David, as He spoke through His holy prophets, those of ages past, salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us, to show mercy to our fathers and to remember His holy covenant, the oath He swore to our father Abraham, to grant us deliverance from hostile hands, that we may serve Him without fear, in holiness and righteousness before Him all the days of our lives.
passages.sermon:
God acted for His people Israel.
God raised up a horn of salvation for us.
God did this in the house of His servant David.
God spoke about this through His holy prophets.
God’s prophets spoke long ago.
God promised salvation from our enemies.
God promised rescue from all who hate us.
God wanted to show mercy to our fathers.
God remembered His holy covenant.
God made an oath to Abraham, our father.
God swore to give us deliverance from hostile hands.
God rescued us so we can serve Him without fear.
God wants us to serve Him in holiness.
God wants us to serve Him in righteousness.
God wants us to serve Him before His presence.
God wants us to do this all the days of our lives.
passages.original: καὶ ἤγειρεν κέρας σωτηρίας ἡμῖν ἐν οἴκῳ Δαυὶδ παιδὸς αὐτοῦ καθὼς ἐλάλησεν διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπ’ αἰῶνος προφητῶν αὐτοῦ σωτηρίαν ἐξ ἐχθρῶν ἡμῶν καὶ ἐκ χειρὸς πάντων τῶν μισούντων ἡμᾶς ποιῆσαι ἔλεος μετὰ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν καὶ μνησθῆναι διαθήκης ἁγίας αὐτοῦ ὅρκον ὃν ὤμοσεν πρὸς Ἀβραὰμ τὸν πατέρα ἡμῶν τοῦ δοῦναι ἡμῖν ἀφόβως ἐκ χειρὸς ἐχθρῶν ῥυσθέντας λατρεύειν αὐτῷ ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πάσαις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἡμῶν

passages.text: And you, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High; for you will go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him, to give to His people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins, because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the Dawn will visit us from on high, to shine on those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the path of peace.”
passages.sermon:
You are a child.
You will be called a prophet of the Most High God.
You will go before the Lord.
You will prepare the way for the Lord.
You will give knowledge of salvation to His people.
You will do this by telling them about the forgiveness of their sins.
God will forgive their sins because He is full of tender mercy.
Because of God's mercy, the Dawn from on high will visit us.
The Dawn will shine on people who live in darkness.
The Dawn will shine on those who sit in the shadow of death.
The Dawn will guide our feet into the path of peace.
passages.original: Καὶ σὺ δέ παιδίον προφήτης Ὑψίστου κληθήσῃ προπορεύσῃ γὰρ ἐνώπιον Κυρίου ἑτοιμάσαι ὁδοὺς αὐτοῦ τοῦ δοῦναι γνῶσιν σωτηρίας τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ ἐν ἀφέσει ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν διὰ σπλάγχνα ἐλέους Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐν οἷς ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους ἐπιφᾶναι τοῖς ἐν σκότει καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου καθημένοις τοῦ κατευθῦναι τοὺς πόδας ἡμῶν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰρήνης

passages.text: And the child grew and became strong in spirit; and he lived in the wilderness until the time of his public appearance to Israel.
passages.sermon:
The child grew.
The child became strong in spirit.
The child lived in the wilderness.
He stayed there until the day he appeared publicly to Israel.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ παιδίον ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐκραταιοῦτο πνεύματι καὶ ἦν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις ἕως ἡμέρας ἀναδείξεως αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ
